title: When the Late Window Starts for a Holder Refund
content:
# When the Late Window Starts for a Holder Refund

Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda refunds released to the holder count their refund payment period, and any late days, from the start of the late window. Where that window starts turns on two records: whether the waiver's purchase deal stands unwound in the Vehicle Purchase Agreements records (its status and its closed date), and how the effective date of the waiver's ending (the waiver's closing date) compares with the loan payoff date the lienholder reported.

**Rule**

- Where the waiver's purchase deal stands unwound, the late window starts on that deal's closed date, the date it was unwound.
- Where the deal is not unwound and the effective date of the waiver's ending is earlier than the loan payoff date, the late window starts on the loan payoff date, the day the lienholder's payoff report reached the waiver.
- In every other case the late window starts on the effective date of the waiver's ending.

**Timeline cases (hypothetical days)**

| Deal unwound? | Effective date of ending | Loan payoff date | Window starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes, unwound on Day 3 | Day 5 | Day 5 | Day 3 |
| No | Day 10 | Day 25 | Day 25 |
| No | Day 25 | Day 25 | Day 25 (the effective date) |
| No | Day 31 | Day 25 | Day 31 (the effective date) |

Where the deal is not unwound, the window therefore starts on the later of the effective date of the waiver's ending and the loan payoff date; equal dates give the same day either way.
